reason: The submitted 1.86% is proved only for an additional loading/activation model. The source says 10 mg of C3N4 and gives a 3.8% catalyst mass fraction; the candidate instead treats 10 mg as total loaded-composite mass and sets catalyst mass to 0.038×10 mg. Under the standard mass-fraction definition, catalyst mass is 0.038/(1−0.038)×10 mg, producing 1.9328587956…% (1.93% at three significant figures). It also equates all loaded catalyst molecules with active catalyst molecules without source data on the active fraction. Moreover, the aggregate Lean library does not build because IChO2026Problems/All.lean is missing.

coverage.evidence: The theorem directly compiles and proves the candidate-defined raw value 18940872892793693114789369/10186495312500000000000000% and its report as 1.86%. However, catalystAmount_mol is defined as supportBatchMass_g × catalystMassFraction / molarMass, baking in the unsupported interpretation that the printed 10 mg of C3N4 is total composite mass. The result is valid only under that extra convention and an assumed active fraction of one.

unsupported_assumptions: The printed 10 mg of C3N4 is treated as 10 mg of total catalyst-loaded composite, so catalyst mass is taken as 0.038×10 mg. Standard mass fraction is constituent mass divided by total mixture mass; with 10 mg support, the required relation is m_cat/(10 mg+m_cat)=0.038. See [IUPAC Gold Book: mass fraction](https://goldbook.iupac.org.org/terms/view/M03722).

Every loaded molecule of catalyst 1 is assumed to be an active catalyst molecule. The source defines TOF per active molecule but supplies no active fraction or theorem identifying loaded and active populations.
source_checks: TASK.json was read first; it requests only co_quantum_yield in percent, with raw value retained and a three-significant-figure report.
SHA-256 hashes of theory_problem.pdf, T8_page-1.png, and T8_page-2.png match TASK.json and isolation_manifest.json.

Original PDF pages Q8-1/Q8-2 and both supplied T8 page images were visually inspected. They confirm 390 nm, 50 mW, TOF 8 h⁻¹, 10 mg of C3N4, catalyst mass fraction 3.8%, molar mass 557.21 g mol⁻¹, and the electron/photon quantum-yield formula.
Blank student sheet A8-5 on PDF page 81 was visually inspected; it contains only blank fields for Ncat and φ and supplies no additional datum.
The acidic half-reaction requires two electrons per CO. Photon-energy, time-unit, and exact-SI-constant arithmetic in the candidate is otherwise consistent.

Independent exact arithmetic reproduces 1.859410161368362…% under the candidate's altered 0.038×10 mg convention and 1.932858795601208…% under the standard mass-fraction relation for 10 mg of support.
proof_checks: The printed final theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound; no custom axiom or sorryAx appears.
Candidate Lean sources contain no sorry, admit, unsafe declaration, custom axiom, or native_decide.
lake build IChO2026Problems fails because IChO2026Problems.lean imports the missing IChO2026Problems/All.lean, so the submitted project lacks a clean aggregate build.

The final proof unfolds electronsPerCO := 2 directly. co_half_reaction_balanced is only an unlabeled conjunction of elementary arithmetic identities, and electron_coefficient_from_charge_balance is not used to derive the factor in the final theorem.
The key unsupported loading relation is hidden inside catalystAmount_mol rather than exposed as a premise, so the final theorem does not establish the source-defined quantity unconditionally.
